paper_title: Strong (D)QBF Dependency Schemes via Pure Paths with Applications to Proof Checking
statement: 5.2 Qute + D∀pure While we have motivated this work on proof checking, we were interested in the solving capabilities of D∀pure . To this end we integrated D∀pure into the dependency learning solver Qute. As with Drrs , it is unknown whether Qute can soundly use D∀pure for term learning (to prove truth of formulas), so we only turn on D∀pure for clause learning.
context: More experiments will be interesting to evaluate the performance of DQRAT-check in different scenarios, but for them to be practical, it is first necessary to develop certifying DQBF solvers that output proofs, ideally taking advantage of all DQRAT rules. 5.2 Qute + D∀pure While we have motivated this work on proof checking, we were interested in the solving capabilities of D∀pure . To this end we integrated D∀pure into the dependency learning solver Qute. As with Drrs , it is unknown whether Qute can soundly use D∀pure for term learning (to prove truth of formulas), so we only turn on D∀pure for clause learning. We found D∀pure detects no independence on the newest QBFEval 2022 benchmarks, and Qute performs better without the overhead of Drrs or D∀pure . On QBFEval 2020 benchmarks D∀pure shows promise: compared to Drrs , 7× less time is spent on computing dependencies, 2× more independent pairs are found, and 3× more D∀pure reductions are executed (geometric means), but this did not yield more solved instances or better PAR2 score. For ts-LQParity formulas which separate Drrs from D∀pure Qute +D∀pure performs well as expected. 6 Conclusion

paper_title: Strong (D)QBF Dependency Schemes via Pure Paths with Applications to Proof Checking
statement: We have shown that DQRAT+D∀pure is p-equivalent to IndExtQURes, and thus a number of useful p-simulations via transitivity. What we cannot show by transitivity is a p-simulation of the newly created LD-Q(D∀pure )-Res, because long-distance resolution steps do not have a sound meaning in DQBF. Nonetheless we conjecture such a p-simulation will exist and we point to the literature [28, 16, 37] that demonstrate that there are a variety of successful of formalisations and p-simulations of long-distance resolution. We aim to further improve and explore the capabilities of our prototype proof checker DQRAT-check.
